beats.say: Orban, a Hungarian master, shipped a 20-ton bombard from Constantinople's own walls, startling the defenders.
The massive stone ball, 600 kilograms, cracked the Theodosian walls within hours, a sound like thunder.
Meanwhile, Emperor Constantine XI secretly offered Sultan Mehmed a 200,000-gold-piece loan, hoping to buy time.
Mehmed refused, yet the promise of wealth fueled his troops, turning greed into relentless fire.
Janissaries unleashed the first coordinated volley of cannons, a thunderous chorus that rattled the Golden Horn.
By night, the Ottoman navy used grappling hooks to pull ships alongside, boarding the weakened sea walls.
Inside, the Byzantine garrison, outnumbered, resorted to boiling oil, but the new cannon's blast melted it.
At dawn, the final breach opened; Mehmed entered, shouting "the city is mine!" as walls fell.
The Hagia Sophia's dome, once a beacon, echoed with the clang of Ottoman drums, sealing destiny.
By sunset, the flag of the rising empire fluttered over the Golden Gate, ending an empire of 1,100 years.
